Paragraph: After the Kurukshetra war, King Yudhishthira was consumed by intense grief and guilt over the massive loss of life, feeling unworthy to rule. Sage Vyasa and Bhishma (lying on his bed of arrows) provided compassionate wisdom, explaining the complexities of duty, destiny, and repentance, helping Yudhishthira release his guilt and accept his royal responsibilities.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Post-traumatic guilt, survivor guilt, depression following victory, and feeling unworthy to lead.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Elders engage in extensive grief counseling and moral education, normalizing his pain while guiding him toward self-forgiveness and duty.
Outcome/Resolution: Yudhisthira recovers from acute depression, embraces self-forgiveness, and assumes the throne to heal his kingdom.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Shanti-Upadesha (Teachings on restoring peace to a traumatized mind)
Raja-Dharma (Re-engaging with societal duty to heal personal grief)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: True repentance transforms guilt into compassionate action, allowing one to serve society with a healed heart.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: A model for treating trauma, survivor guilt, and existential depression through mentorship and community duty.
